Tidy, glance at and plot a Bayesian VAR

Source: R/bvar-plot.R
tidy.bvarm.Rd

tidy() summarises the posterior of the coefficients: response, term, estimate (posterior mean), std.error (posterior sd), conf.low, conf.high (equal-tailed interval). glance() is a one-row summary: K, p, nobs, ndraw, method, logml, accept, plus the posterior means of the hyperparameters when they were estimated.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'bvarm'
tidy(x, conf.level = 0.9, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bvarm'
as_tibble(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bvarm'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bvarm'
autoplot(object, type = c("coef", "hyper", "trace"), conf.level = 0.9, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bvarm'
plot(x, ...)

Arguments

x, object

a bvarm() fit.

conf.level

credible level of the interval (default 0.90).

...

unused (plot() passes them to autoplot()).

type

"coef", "hyper" or "trace".

Value

tidy(), glance(): a tibble; autoplot(): a ggplot.

Details

autoplot() shows the coefficient intervals (type = "coef"), the posterior densities of the hyperparameters ("hyper") or their trace plots ("trace"; the coefficient draws if there are no hyperparameters).

See also

Other Bayesian VAR: autoplot.mcmc_diagnostics(), bvarm(), mcmc_diagnostics(), prior_minnesota(), prior_triangular(), volatility()

Examples

# \donttest{
fit <- bvarm(yraw, p = 2, ndraw = 500, nburn = 300)
tidy(fit)
#> # A tibble: 21 × 6
#>    response term     estimate std.error  conf.low conf.high
#>    <chr>    <chr>       <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>
#>  1 infl     infl.l1    1.53      0.0593  1.43       1.61   
#>  2 infl     unemp.l1  -0.258     0.0595 -0.351     -0.161  
#>  3 infl     rate.l1   -0.0460    0.0282 -0.0904    -0.00161
#>  4 infl     infl.l2   -0.531     0.0615 -0.626     -0.435  
#>  5 infl     unemp.l2   0.219     0.0576  0.128      0.312  
#>  6 infl     rate.l2    0.0461    0.0273 -0.000270   0.0881 
#>  7 infl     const      0.246     0.0914  0.0904     0.400  
#>  8 unemp    infl.l1    0.0186    0.0632 -0.0837     0.118  
#>  9 unemp    unemp.l1   1.33      0.0641  1.23       1.44   
#> 10 unemp    rate.l1   -0.0220    0.0293 -0.0689     0.0276 
#> # ℹ 11 more rows
glance(fit)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 10
#>       K     p  nobs ndraw method        logml accept lambda   soc   sur
#>   <int> <int> <int> <int> <chr>         <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1     3     2   213   500 niw-minnesota -406.  0.556  0.747 0.405 0.885
autoplot(fit, "hyper")

# }
